arxiv-1502-00070.title: Matings of Cubic polynomials with a fixed critical point, Part I: Thurston Obstructions
arxiv-1502-00070.creator: Thomas Sharland
arxiv-1502-00070.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by Thomas Sharland. We prove that if F F is a degree 3 3 Thurston map with two fixed critical points, then any irreducible obstruction for F F contains a Levy cycle. As a corollary, it will be shown that if f f and g g are two postcritically finite cubic polynomials each having a fixed critical point, then any obstruction to the mating f ⟂ ⟂ g f\perp\!\!\!\perp g contains a Levy cycle.

arxiv-1906-09253.title: Variational Quantum Fidelity Estimation
arxiv-1906-09253.creator: M. Cerezo, Alexander Poremba, Lukasz Cincio, Patrick J. Coles
arxiv-1906-09253.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by M. Cerezo, Alexander Poremba, Lukasz Cincio, Patrick J. Coles. Computing quantum state fidelity will be important to verify and characterize states prepared on a quantum computer. In this work, we propose novel lower and upper bounds for the fidelity F ⁡ ( ρ , σ ) F(\rho,\sigma) based on the “truncated fidelity” F ⁡ ( ρ m , σ ) F(\rho_{m},\sigma) , which is evaluated for a state ρ m \rho_{m} obtained by projecting ρ \rho onto its m m -largest eigenvalues.

arxiv-2207-06703.title: Ultra-coherent nanomechanical resonators based on density phononic crystal engineering
arxiv-2207-06703.creator: Dennis Høj, Ulrich Busk Hoff, Ulrik Lund Andersen
arxiv-2207-06703.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dennis Høj, Ulrich Busk Hoff, Ulrik Lund Andersen. Micro- and nanomechanical systems with exceptionally low dissipation rates are enabling the next-generation technologies of ultra-sensitive detectors and quantum information systems. New techniques and methods for lowering the dissipation rate have in recent years been discovered and allowed for the engineering of mechanical oscillators with phononic modes that are extremely well isolated from the environment and thus possessing quality factors close to and beyond 1 billion.

arxiv-2210-08459.title: StoryER: Automatic Story Evaluation via Ranking, Rating and Reasoning
arxiv-2210-08459.creator: Hong Chen, Duc Minh Vo, Hiroya Takamura, Yusuke Miyao, Hideki Nakayama, The University of Tokyo, Tokyo Institute of Technology, National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science, Technology, Japan {chen, vmduc, nakayama}@nlab.ci.i.u-tokyo.ac.jpyusuke@is.s.u-tokyo.ac.jptakamura.hiroya@aist.go.jp
arxiv-2210-08459.description: Abstract Existing automatic story evaluation methods place a premium on story lexical level coherence, deviating from human preference. We go beyond this limitation by considering a novel Story E valuation method that mimics human preference when judging a story, namely StoryER , which consists of three sub-tasks: R anking, R ating and R easoning.

pmc-10632505.title: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor regulates IL-22 receptor expression on thymic epithelial cell and accelerates thymus regeneration
pmc-10632505.creator: Jingyi Shen, Ying Wang, Fei Zheng, Shuo Cao, Qiu Lan, Kailin Xu, Bin Pan
pmc-10632505.description: Improving regeneration of damaged thymus is important for reconstituting T-cell immunity. Interleukin-22 (IL-22) was proved to improve thymus regeneration through recovering thymic epithelial cells (TECs). The IL-22 receptor IL-22RA1 is crucial for mediating IL-22 functions. Mechanism that regulates IL-22RA1 expression is unknown.

pmc-10705126.title: Immunoassay Urine Drug Testing among Patients Receiving Opioids at a Safety-Net Palliative Medicine Clinic
pmc-10705126.creator: John M. Halphen, Joseph A. Arthur, Soraira Pacheco, Linh M. T. Nguyen, Nikitha N. Samy, Nathaniel R. Wilson, Gregory Sattler, Shane E. Wing, Rex A. D. Paulino, Christine Feng, Pulin Shah, Simbiat Olayiwola, Bradley Cannell, Supriyanka Addimulam, Riddhi Patel, David Hui
pmc-10705126.description: Simple SummaryA urine drug test (UDT) is often used in the treatment of cancer pain to monitor compliance with opioid treatment. Two types of UDT are commonly for this purpose: the immunoassay test, and the mass spectrometry method. Only a few studies have examined the use of immunoassay UDT for cancer patients in palliative care clinics.

pmc-10784868.title: Ascites, Pleural, and Pericardial Effusion in Primary Hypothyroidism: A Rare Case Report
pmc-10784868.creator: Pedro Gomes Santos, Roberto Calças Marques, Pedro Martins dos Santos, Catarina Carreira da Costa, Mihail Mogildea
pmc-10784868.description: Hypothyroidism is caused by a deficiency of thyroid hormones and is a common endocrine disorder worldwide. It can affect nearly every organ, resulting in multiple clinical manifestations. Ascites, pleural effusion, and pericardial effusion, although less frequent than peripheral edema, can also be present.

pmc-11227630.creator: Abbey Mkpe, Amadi Simeon Chijioke, Olufemi Adebari Oloyede, Rose Sitonma Iwo-Amah, Paul Ledee Kua, Eghuan Kenneth1 Okagua, Basil Omieibi Altraide, Faithwin Horsfall, Esther Ijeoma Nonye-Enyidah, Ngozi Joseph Kwosah, Alpheaus Gogo Mba, Uduak Solomon Ocheche, Leesi Sapira-Ordu, Dickson H John, Nestor
pmc-11227630.description: Background:There is a paucity of organized human biomonitoring, including that of carbon monoxide (CO) in the Niger Delta, Nigeria. The study aims to quantify the impact of maternal exposure to CO in the first trimester of pregnancy and its modification by maternal demographic and obstetric factors.

pmc-11416908.title: Evolution of the Cytomegalovirus RL11 gene family in Old World monkeys and Great Apes
pmc-11416908.creator: Ulad Litvin, Eddie C Y Wang, Richard J Stanton, Ceri A Fielding, Joseph Hughes
pmc-11416908.description: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is a genus of herpesviruses, members of which share a long history of coevolution with their primate hosts including New World monkeys, Old World monkeys (OWMs), and Great Apes (GAs). These viruses are ubiquitous within their host populations and establish lifelong infection in most individuals.

pmc-11734754.title: Rnalib: a Python library for custom transcriptomics analyses
pmc-11734754.creator: Niko Popitsch, Stefan L Ameres, Peter Robinson
pmc-11734754.description: MotivationThe efficient and reproducible analysis of high-throughput sequencing datasets necessitates the development of methodical and robust computational pipelines that integrate established and bespoke bioinformatics analysis tools, often written in high-level programming languages such as Python. Despite the increasing availability of programming libraries for genomics, there is a noticeable lack of tools specifically focused on transcriptomics.

pmc-12616361.title: Integrating space, time, and culture in animal conservation practice
pmc-12616361.creator: William K Oestreich, Dawn R Barlow, Taylor A Hersh
pmc-12616361.description: Recent theoretical integration of the spatiotemporal and cultural elements of animal behavior has led to increasing calls to incorporate animal culture into conservation. Implementation of this idea remains sparse due to disconnects between the theoretical concept of considering culture in animal conservation and the spatiotemporal approaches typically employed in conservation practice.

pmc-13037767.title: Determining a Likely Mechanism of Missingness in Repeated Measures Sleep Data From Wearable Fitness Trackers: Longitudinal Analysis
pmc-13037767.creator: Kate Mobley, Kevin B Gittner, Karen Nielsen, Lauren M Matheny, Gita Taasoobshirazi, Charles Natuhamya, Monica H Swahn, Georgian Badicu
pmc-13037767.description: BackgroundWearable fitness trackers have become a valuable tool in public health research due to their ability to collect large-scale, individual-level data at a low cost. Because of this, wearables have the potential to mitigate the urgent need for health research in low-resource settings.

pmc-13301943.title: Upgrading to biventricular pacing or left bundle branch area pacing in the treatment of pacemaker-induced cardiomyopathy
pmc-13301943.creator: M Dogan, U Canpolat, A Kivrak, A H Ates, K Aytemir
pmc-13301943.description: BackgroundPacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PiCM) is a recognized complication of chronic right ventricular (RV) pacing, yet optimal management remains debated. Upgrading to biventricular pacing (BiVP) or left bundle branch area pacing (LBBaP) may reverse dysfunction, but comparative data are limited.ObjectiveTo compare the efficacy and safety of upgrading to BiVP versus LBBaP in patients with PiCM.

pmc-13458801.title: Pacing cessation just before generator replacement - A life-threatening consequence of pacemaker battery depletion: A case report
pmc-13458801.creator: Ryoto Mitsumizo, Yusuke Takahara, Hiroshi Ikuta, Ryota Komoto, Ryuichi Matsukawa, Keita Inanaga, Jun-ichiro Nishi
pmc-13458801.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We report the case of a 77-year-old man who underwent single-chamber pacemaker implantation 16 years prior. The patient, who did not utilize remote monitoring, was lost to follow-up 14 years after the implantation, leading to profound battery depletion. This lack of surveillance resulted in a critical reduction of the pacing rate to 14 ppm, culminating in the complete cessation of pacing immediately before generator replacement. Despite the Abbott device's specified End-of-Life (EOL) safety mechanism, pacing function failed entirely—a rare but life-threatening complication.
